## Kestrel Bastion 1500 Review: 4/5 — It Saved My 10x Long, But It Won't Run My Whole Desk

I bought the Kestrel Bastion 1500 off Voltwise in August 2026 for $229. The reason I needed it is simple: my apartment loses power more often than I'd like, and I trade leveraged. What I didn't expect was that I'd end up using it for the one job that actually matters — keeping my rig and my internet alive long enough to get out of a position cleanly.

### The numbers

| Spec | Detail |
|---|---|
| Capacity | 1500VA / 1000W, pure sine wave |
| My measured load | ~410W (PC + 3 monitors + modem + router, read off its own display) |
| Actual runtime at 410W | 11 min 40 sec (tested by pulling the plug on purpose) |
| Box claim | ~14 min at 500W |
| Outlets | 10 — 5 battery-backed, 5 surge-only |
| USB-C | 60W |
| Weight | ~30 lbs |
| Replacement battery pack | $95 |

Here's the math the box doesn't do for you: "14 min at 500W" implies roughly 117Wh of usable energy. My actual result — 410W for 11 min 40 sec — works out to about 80Wh delivered. So the sticker number is optimistic. Plan on ~80Wh. At a genuine 500W you'd get closer to 10 minutes, not 14. Either way, treat it as a "close out and shut down" device, not a "keep working" device.

### October 14

Power dropped around 2:20pm. I was 10x long SOL perps. The rig stayed up, the wifi stayed up, and I closed the position in about 4 minutes with room to spare. No panic-click, no scrambling to find a hotspot. One avoided bad fill, and the unit paid for itself on that afternoon alone.

### What bugs me about it

- **The fan.** First week, the fan kicked on at 3am and woke me up. It's loud — like a hair dryer on low — and it cycles more than I'd like under sustained load. If your desk is in your bedroom, know this going in.
- **The beeping.** On outage it's loud af. You *can* mute it in the app, but the setting resets after a firmware update. Re-mute it every time or you're awake at 3am.
- **The desktop app looks like Windows XP.** Auto-shutdown works, and that's what I actually care about, but the UI hasn't been touched in a decade. Don't expect a polished battery dashboard.
- **$95 for a replacement battery pack**, on top of the $229. If you're buying this as multi-year outage insurance, factor that in, plus the fact that degradation in 3-4 years hits your wallet.
- **30 lbs.** Don't plan on moving it around. Put it next to your desk, near an outlet, since it needs wall power to recharge.
- **Only 5 of the 10 outlets are battery-backed.** Plugging your PC into a surge-only outlet is the classic screw-up: the lights come on, you assume you're protected, and you're not.

### Tips if you get one

- **Put the modem and router on the battery-backed side.** People forget this and lose internet even though the PC is fine. My number one tip.
- **Need more minutes?** Drop a monitor's brightness to zero or shut one off entirely. That load cut extends runtime more than anything else.
- **Set the auto-shutdown threshold in the app now**, and test it once on purpose like I did. You want to know it works before the outage, not during it.
- **Test the runtime with your own gear.** The sticker doesn't know your load.

### Who it's for

Traders running a desktop rig and a couple of monitors who need a few minutes to flatten a position and shut down cleanly, with internet kept alive through it. If you need 30+ minutes of runtime, or you have a server that genuinely has to stay up, step up to a 2000W+ unit or a second battery pack. If you're in an area with frequent outages and need real multi-hour runtime, a small generator is the better buy. This is a "don't get wrecked" device.

### Verdict

**4/5.** It did exactly what I needed on Oct 14, and the fan noise and ugly app are real complaints but minor next to what it bought me. The only thing I actually want changed is the beep resetting after firmware updates — and honestly, another 20 minutes of runtime would make this a 5.
